source.title: Getting ViT in Shape: Scaling Laws for Compute-Optimal Model Design
source.authors: Ibrahim M. Alabdulmohsin; Xiao-Hua Zhai; Alexander Kolesnikov; Lucas Beyer

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study develops and tests scaling-law methods on vision transformers, a modality outside the claim’s language-model setting. It reports fitted scaling exponents and compute-related predictions for vision tasks.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses and cites language-model scaling laws but does not run language models or measure held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. Its fitted measures are downstream image-classification error or image-to-text perplexity. Results quoted from cited work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits joint power-law scaling forms for ViTs pretrained on JFT-3B and evaluated downstream (ImageNet few-shot error, image-to-text perplexity), reports data and compute-optimal shape exponents, and checks prediction on a held-out point. These results bear on whether scaling-law forms hold beyond text (V5), on downstream predictability (V6), on fit dependence (V7), and through shape comparisons on V4 in a vision setting. It runs no language models and reports no held-out LM pretraining loss, so V1, V2 and V3 as stated for LMs are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that jointly optimising ViT shape (width, depth, MLP dim) and training duration for compute lets smaller models (e.g. SoViT-400m/14) match much larger ones. They report that their star-plus-grid sweep cuts the number of experiments needed and gives near-identical shape exponents for classification and image-to-text. They add that shape matters in vision, unlike LM upstream findings, and that their results agree partially with Chinchilla. They note panoptic segmentation as a limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses a vision-specific joint fit over architecture dimensions and downstream metrics, with star and grid sweeps; it does not reproduce language-model held-out pretraining-loss measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: Some fitted exponents vary with evaluation metric; small-model optimal shapes differ between image classification and image-to-text tasks. The paper says compute-optimal dimension exponents are comparatively robust across the tested metrics and nearly identical across the two domains.

fits_no_version.finding: The compute-optimal shape found for classification transfers to most tasks but underperforms on panoptic segmentation (43.7 vs 44.8 PQ for ViT-g/14). In small models, optimal shapes differ between classification and image-to-text tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal architecture shapes derived from one downstream metric transfer imperfectly across task domains.

record.problems: The study is in vision rather than language modeling and uses downstream error or perplexity rather than held-out language-model pretraining cross-entropy. The prediction comparison is presented graphically without numerical predicted-versus-actual values in the text. It does not report optimal token counts or a direct parameter-versus-token allocation trend.
record.rows_left_out: Broad benchmark comparisons and model-transfer results were omitted because they do not fit or test a scaling law. Figure 6’s separate shape-deviation results were not extracted as rows because the text gives no separate numerical values for each deviation and the comparison is not at fixed parameter count.

untested.parts: All: no language models and no held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
Extrapolation of LM pretraining loss across orders of magnitude. The vision check is downstream, figure-only, and within one sweep's range.
LM compute-optimal parameter and token counts and their relative growth. No token or data-allocation exponent is reported even for ViT.
Upstream LM loss at fixed parameter count. Only one same-size vision comparison exists (B-150m vs SoViT-150m).
Video, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer scaling regimes.
LM downstream tasks and prediction from pretraining loss.
Parameter counting, training schedule, data and fitting-method effects on LM laws; curvature away from a single power law.

missing.what: B-150m (ViT-B shape, same size as SoViT-150m) vs SoViT-150m at equal compute: 77.9% vs 78.5% ImageNet 10-shot. This is a fixed-parameter shape comparison.
Grid sweep showing shape changes downstream error at fixed compute (600M examples), with different optimal shapes for classification and image-to-text.
IsoFLOP curves over width are non-monotone (quasiconvex) at fixed compute, matching the LM compute-frontier behaviour.

record.verdict_notes: All results are vision and downstream metrics. V1–V3 as stated for LMs are untested. The V2 and V3 links in the record were removed because the system kind differs (ViT, not LM) and the held-out check is not orders of magnitude out. The V4 verdict rests on text not captured in the rows.

versions.untested_parts: No language models or held-out pretraining cross-entropy; the paper’s vision results do not test the stated language-model loss relation.
Tests extrapolation for vision-task metrics, not language-model pretraining loss or runs orders of magnitude larger in language-model scale.
Reports a compute-related parameter-count trend for vision models, but does not directly report optimal language-model parameter and token counts or their relative growth.
The shape comparisons do not hold parameter count fixed; some instead hold compute fixed.
Tests vision transformers and image-to-text decoding, not image/video model families generally, repeated data, or a broad set of training regimes.
Tests downstream vision metrics, not language-model downstream tasks or prediction from language-model pretraining loss.
Tests metric and domain dependence of fitted vision scaling exponents; does not test the causes of disagreement between the cited language-model laws or systematic bending of language-model curves.

tranche.reason: The study tests scaling forms and compute-optimal architecture scaling in vision using downstream classification and image-to-text metrics, a new setting relative to language-model pretraining loss.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v5, dated January 2024, of the NeurIPS 2023 paper. The reported s_k are individual dimension exponents from Equation (4); distinguish them from parameter/token allocation and the subsequent joint-scaling procedure.

statements.correction: Figure 6: B-150m and SoViT-150m have equal parameter count and compute; ImageNet 10-shot accuracy is 77.9% and 78.5%, respectively. Section 4.1: optimizing shape improves downstream performance. Fixed-parameter loss insensitivity is not measured by this comparison.
statements.problem: The ViT comparison is accurate, but downstream accuracy does not directly test V4's claim about loss.

statements.correction: Sections 3 and 4.1: held-out star centre is (1968, 40, 6144); fitted width, depth and MLP grids reach only 1648, 24 and 3072. Figure 4: the star centre is excluded from parameter estimation; the authors report accurate extrapolation of downstream 10-shot error. This is not an orders-of-magnitude extrapolation test.
statements.problem: Calling the held-out ViT check interpolation conflicts with the fitted shape ranges and the paper's description.
